data.title: Inside VinFast’s Net-Zero Climate Commitment
data.description:
While some automakers have scaled back their North American EV ambitions, VinFast continues to view electric vehicles as essential to addressing climate change. In the U.S. and Canada, the company is focused on making EVs easier to purchase, charge and service while helping customers understand operating costs. Its broader strategy centers on building a network of vehicles, charging infrastructure and services that can support more drivers and fleets over time.

One of the latest steps came on October 6, 2026, when VinFast announced an initial agreement with NexMove at the APTA TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago to bring its electric buses to U.S. customers. NexMove, a joint venture between Transportation Management Services and Zeem Solutions, plans to bundle buses, charging, maintenance and operations in a single agreement. It intends to offer a 97% uptime service-level commitment, with certified bus deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. The announcement followed VinFast’s September 2026 franchise agreements for three U.S. dealerships in California and Pennsylvania.

Making electric mobility practical for fleets and drivers

For a transit agency, introducing electric buses requires decisions about depot charging, maintenance schedules and daily vehicle availability. NexMove’s proposed service brings these elements together into one agreement. Ahead of certified deliveries, NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem’s charging depots, where transit agencies and fleet operators can evaluate the vehicles firsthand. The demonstration units are intended for evaluation, with certified vehicles to follow on the planned delivery schedule.

VinFast’s buses combine camera- and radar-based driver assistance, fast charging capabilities, lithium iron phosphate batteries and corrosion protection. The company reported that approximately 2,000 of its electric buses were operating in Vietnam at the time of the announcement. VinFast’s experience in the market spans manufacturing, operations and maintenance, giving it firsthand knowledge of the demands fleet operators face when vehicles are in daily service.

“Bringing VinFast electric buses to the United States marks an important next step in our long-term commitment to this market,” said Brian Finnerty, CEO of VinFast North America.

For households, the questions are more personal: How much will it cost to charge a vehicle each month? Where can it be serviced? What options are available at a price the buyer can afford? The franchise agreements in Redondo Beach and Tustin, California, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, expand access to sales and after-sales service. The company’s U.S. certified pre-owned program gives buyers another option when weighing the upfront cost of an EV.

In Canada, VinFast offers a 10-year or 200,000-kilometre limited new-vehicle warranty on the VF 8, whichever comes first. Its online energy-cost calculator allows shoppers to compare estimated EV charging costs with the fueling costs of a gasoline vehicle over their expected mileage and ownership period. The comparison gives buyers a clearer picture of how an EV could fit their driving habits and household budget.

Annual EV charging costs can be 50% or more below gasoline fueling costs, depending on electricity rates, whether drivers charge at home or use public stations, driving habits, and vehicle efficiency. Coltura’s Q3 2024 analysis estimated that U.S. EV drivers saved an average of 7.4 cents per mile on fuel. At 1,200 miles a month, that works out to about $90 a month, or nearly $1,100 a year if the same per-mile savings hold.

Why a long-term climate commitment matters as markets change

VinFast announced its transition to all-electric vehicle production at CES in Las Vegas in 2022. Just over two years later, it became Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle brand in 2024, according to Vingroup’s annual report. Its expansion into North America brings a different set of considerations, including where to build out sales and service operations, how to support charging infrastructure and how to help commercial customers integrate electric vehicles into their existing operations.

Incentives, regulations and customer demand can change while a factory upgrade or charging project is still in development. VinFast’s 2040 net-zero goal provides a long-term framework for investments that take years to plan and implement. For example, the timing of an equipment replacement affects when a plant can shift more of its operations to electricity. The source of that electricity then affects the emissions associated with running the equipment. Decisions about materials and suppliers have a similar bearing on emissions across the value chain.

VinFast’s emissions inventory illustrates why those decisions matter as production grows. The company calculated that its emissions exceeded 1.12 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in its 2022 base year. In a separate scenario, VinFast estimated that emissions could exceed 20 million metric tons of CO₂e if its existing production operations in Vietnam reached their maximum registered capacity, excluding future factories. The estimate illustrates the importance of factoring energy efficiency, electricity sourcing and supplier emissions into plans for higher production.

How the 3E Mission puts the 2040 pledge into practice

VinFast signed The Climate Pledge on August 17, 2022, and announced its participation in September 2022. It was the first Vietnamese enterprise to sign the pledge, an initiative co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism. The company’s stated goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, covering direct emissions from its operations, indirect emissions from purchased energy, and emissions across its wider value chain. Signatories commit to measuring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions regularly, reducing emissions and neutralizing the remainder.

In January 2025, VinFast’s chairwoman approved the company’s net-zero strategy through 2030, with a view to 2040. The strategy centers on the 3E Mission, which sets out how VinFast plans to change the equipment it uses, reduce the energy it needs and source cleaner power.

  • Electrification. VinFast plans to electrify equipment at company-owned production and business sites by 2030. The roadmap also includes expanding access to charging and developing battery energy storage.

  • Energy Saving. VinFast plans to introduce smart energy monitoring at manufacturing facilities by 2028. Monitoring production lines and major electricity-consuming equipment gives factory teams more detailed information on where energy is used and where operations can be made more efficient.

  • Energy Greening. VinFast aims to use 100% renewable electricity at all its plants by 2040. Its roadmap includes rooftop solar, battery storage to support renewable power use, and work with suppliers on lower-emission materials.

VinFast’s manufacturing complex in Hai Phong offers a practical example of what these priorities translate to on the factory floor. The company reported that upgrades to lighting and compressed-air systems, changes to how production robots operate, and other efficiency measures saved approximately 2.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, equivalent to an estimated 1,782 metric tons of CO₂e.

The company also said it initiated a 30-megawatt-peak rooftop solar project at the site. While the efficiency measures address how much electricity the plant needs, the solar project addresses the source of the electricity.

Against its 2022 baseline, VinFast aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% and Scope 3 emissions by 29% by 2030. By 2040, the strategy calls for cutting total emissions by at least 85% and neutralizing residual emissions of up to 15% through carbon offsetting mechanisms, which could include carbon credits. As VinFast serves more drivers and fleets, its reported emissions will show how far the company has progressed toward those targets across its operations, purchased energy and value chain.

data.title: Foreign investors post biggest Japanese stock selloff in nine weeks as AI jitters deepen
data.description:
Foreign investors made their biggest Japanese equity sales in nine weeks in the week ended November 20, as a wider selloff in global AI-linked companies and hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials weighed on risk appetite.

They withdrew a net 571.6 billion yen ($3.59 billion) from local stocks, the largest amount for a week since September 19, Ministry of Finance data showed on Friday.

The Nikkei 225 fell 7.7% last week, closing at a seven-month low of 56,436.65. This week, the Nikkei has gained about 3.7% so far.

Global AI-related stocks have come under pressure this month due to concerns about returns on massive investments in the AI buildout as well as the prospect of tighter AI regulation and oversight after Democrats won the US midterm elections.

While the outflows trimmed foreign investors' net purchases of Japanese stocks to 9.99 trillion yen so far this year, they are higher than their net purchases of about 7.64 trillion yen in the same period last year.

Foreigners also bought a net 208.5 billion yen of Japanese long-term bonds, marking an eighth consecutive week of net purchases. They sold a net 1.79 trillion yen of short-term bills.

Meanwhile, Japanese investors bought a net 423.5 billion yen of foreign long-term bonds, ending a two-week streak of net selling. They also purchased a net 15.8 billion yen of short-term bills.

Japanese investors sold a net 350.8 billion yen of overseas equities, reversing nearly all of the 363.1 billion yen in net purchases recorded the previous week.

($1 = 159.2800 yen)

data.title: Conservatives would win election in Australia's second state, says poll
data.description:
Australia's centre-right conservatives look set for a decisive win at an election in the state of Victoria on Saturday, a new poll showed, ending more than a decade of state Labor government and seeing off populist right-wing challengers.

An election result in line with the poll in the country's second-most populous state would reassure establishment parties that a surge in support for Pauline Hanson's One Nation, Australia's answer to US President Donald Trump, Alternative for Germany and Reform UK, does not translate to votes at scale.

The Newspoll published on Friday said the Liberal-National coalition led by Jess Wilson, 36, came in ahead of Labor 57.5% to 42.5% when counting for likely voter preferences. That would hand the conservatives up to 67 of the state's 88 lower house seats, the poll said.

If that pattern is repeated at the ballot, the Victorian Labor party would win just 17 seats, from 54 currently, the poll showed, which would be the party's worst showing on record.

A conservative win would close the book on a government which rode high in the polls for years — even through some of the world's longest COVID lockdowns, in its capital city Melbourne — but which has become deeply unpopular as voters fret over worsening affordability and new taxes intended to pay down the highest state debt in the country.

It would also sound the alarm for Labor governments in larger New South Wales state, which faces an election in March, and federally, where an election is due by 2028.

One Nation was formed by maverick Hanson in 1997 on an anti-immigration platform and remained at the political fringes until May 2025, when a resounding defeat in a national election threw the federal conservative coalition into crisis. Hanson's party won just 6% of the vote at that election but by year-end was leading some polls.

This May, the party won its first federal lower house seat in a byelection, in a regional New South Wales seat that borders Victoria. The party ran just five lower house candidates in Victoria in 2022, winning none, but has run candidates in all 88 seats in 2026.

Under Australia's preferential ballot system, if no candidate wins a majority, the contender with the lowest count is eliminated and their votes are distributed to the person their supporters nominated as their next preference.

data.title: Malaysia's Large-Cap Contractors Likely Insulated From Nvidia Shipment Halt — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's large-cap contractors should be relatively insulated from the impact of Nvidia's reported halt on server shipments to Southeast Asia, given their data center exposure is weighted toward U.S. hyperscalers, Citi analyst Steven Chan says in a note. He sees no delays to existing projects but flags potential risks to future tenders from 2H 2027 onward. Non-hyperscaler customers, including cloud providers and colocation operators, are likely to be more affected by Nvidia's move, he adds. Chan remains cautious on the broader data center sector, as China-linked demand accounts for a significant share of capacity and future projects. Operators and contractors outside the U.S. hyperscaler ecosystem could face risks of slower project conversion, tighter financing and pressured valuations, Citi adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: Indian shares muted as IT pullback offsets broader gains
data.description:
By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M

Indian shares slipped marginally on Friday, as IT stocks dropped after a four-session rally to offset broader gains from returning foreign inflows.

The Nifty 50 slipped 0.16% to 25,845.1 while the Sensex eased 0.29% to 84,077.8, as of 10:03 a.m. IST.

Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged gains. The broader small-caps and mid-caps gained about 1% each.

The 50-stock Nifty index and the Sensex are up 0.2% each so far this week, consolidating after a nearly 15% surge over the last four weeks that saw Indian benchmarks outperforming Asian and emerging market peers.

The rally in November was driven by record monthly foreign inflows, worth $15.5 billion, aided by a global AI trade reversal and robust earnings.

Brent crude futures hovered around $96.5 per barrel, rising 4.2% over the week as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from the conflict-hit region.

"The rise in Brent crude is negative news in the context of rising inflation in India, while the US tariff proposal is another threat," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.

After the recent rally, "a consolidation phase appears likely in the near term," Vijayakumar said.

IT index fell 1.5% after rising 8% in the last four sessions.

Among stocks, Waaree Renewable Technologies surged 10% after receiving a letter of award for a 120 MWp turnkey EPC project.

Freight wagon manufacturer Texmaco Rail gained 2.6% on winning an order worth $6.02 million from Utkal Alumina International for supply of 108 railway wagons.

Engineering, procurement and construction firm EMS added 2% on securing a $2.8 million order from the National Highways Authority of India.

Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields (MHAN.NS) fell 1.5% in its trading debutk.

Jet Freight Logistics fell 2% after the logistics firm said India's markets regulator summoned its chairman and managing director as part of an ongoing investigation into the company.

data.title: Price Action: Zydus Lifesciences slips on USFDA CRL; Syrma SGS, Avalon Technologies gain after JPMorgan upgrades
data.description:
Stock-specific action remained in focus on Dalal Street on November 27 with investors reacting to brokerage recommendations and regulatory developments.

Share price of Zydus Lifesciences fell more than 1 percent after its US subsidiary, Zydus Therapeutics Inc., received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) for its New Drug Application (NDA) for Saroglitazar. The letter relates to the company's resolution plan addressing observations raised during the October 2026 inspection of its Moraiya facility.

Shares of Syrma SGS and Avalon Technologies rose nearly 2% each after JPMorgan upgraded the stocks to 'neutral'.

Lemon Tree Hotels share price rose nearly 1 percent after company announced the opening of Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels in Pali. With this addition, the group's operational portfolio in Maharashtra has expanded to 17 hotels, while another 15 properties are in the development pipeline. The property operates under a franchise agreement, further strengthening the group's presence and expanding its development pipeline across the region.

On the sectoral front, Nifty PSU Bank and Metal indices rose more than 1 percent each, while IT index shed 1.6%.

Broader markets traded higher, with the Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices gaining nearly 1 percent each.

Market breadth remained positive on the BSE, with 2314 shares advancing against 995 declining, while 196 stocks remained unchanged.

data.title: Trump says Huang is excited about his 'second term' at Nvidia
data.description:
President Donald Trump said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is happy to return to the role, calling it his “second term,” as the president again defended his intervention in the executive’s reinstatement despite bipartisan national security concerns.

Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thursday, Trump said he had not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced his return but added, “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.”

Trump dismissed concerns surrounding Huang’s reinstatement, saying, “Based on information and belief, I think he’s absolutely fine.” Asked what information he had, Trump offered no specifics, saying only, “The information I have, which is a lot of information.”

Trump had pushed Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang and enlisted Vice President JD Vance to make a personal appeal. The move drew criticism from both parties, with lawmakers calling for scrutiny of Huang’s ties to the administration. Huang is scheduled to testify privately before House lawmakers on Dec. 1 and publicly before the Senate on Dec. 3.

Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday following the announcement but fell more than 9.5% over the next two sessions. Trump said, “I will tell you, the market feels very good about it,” adding that he believed he had done “a great thing for our country and even for the world.”

Trump is scheduled to attend a groundbreaking event for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing chip plant expansion in Arizona on Dec. 4. Asked whether Huang might join him, Trump said, “I would be glad to take him.”
